title.zh: 卷一百一十六 載記第十六 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇
title.en: Volume 116 Records 16: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang
title.raw: 卷一百一十六 載記第十六 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇 Volume 116 Records 16: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲，南安赤亭羌人也。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong was a man of the Qiang of Chiting in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong was a Qiang from Chiting in Nan'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先有虞氏之苗裔。

translations.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Youyu clan.
translations.idiomatic: His line traced back to the house of Youyu.

sentences.zh: 禹封舜少子於西戎，世為羌酋。

translations.literal: Yu enfeoffed Shun's youngest son in the western Rong; for generations they were Qiang chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu enfeoffed Shun’s youngest son among the western tribes, and his descendants became hereditary Qiang chiefs.

sentences.zh: 其後燒當雄於洮、罕之間，七世孫填虞，漢中元末寇擾西州，為楊虛侯馬武所敗，徙出塞。

translations.literal: Afterward Shaodang was mighty between Tao and Han; seventh-generation grandson Dian Yu; late Han Zhongyuan raided and disturbed Western Province; was defeated by Marquis of Yangxu Ma Wu; moved out beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Shaodang branch dominated the Tao and Han rivers; seven generations on, Dian Yu raided Liangzhou in the late Eastern Han until Ma Wu drove the clan beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 虞九世孫遷那率種人內附，漢朝嘉之，假冠軍將軍、西羌校尉、歸順王，處之于南安之赤亭。

translations.literal: Yu's ninth-generation grandson Qianna led tribal people to attach inward; Han court praised him—provisional Champion General, Colonel of the Western Qiang, King of Submission—and settled them at Chiting in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations later Qianna led his people to submit; the Han court named him champion general, colonel of the western Qiang, king of submission, and settled them at Chiting in Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 那玄孫柯回為魏鎮西將軍、綏戎校尉、西羌都督。

translations.literal: Na's great-grandson Kehui was Wei General Who Guards the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, Western Qiang Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant Kehui served Wei as general who guards the west, colonel who pacifies the Rong, and overseer of the western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 回生弋仲，少英毅，不營產業，唯以收恤為務，眾皆畏而親之。

translations.literal: Hui sired Yizhong; from youth heroic and resolute; did not manage estates—only took gathering and relief as task—the multitude all feared yet drew close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Kehui’s son Yao Yizhong was bold in youth, cared nothing for property, and devoted himself to succoring his people, who feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，東徙榆眉，戎夏繈負隨之者數萬，自稱護西羌校尉、雍州刺史、扶風公。

translations.literal: At Yongjia's chaos, east moved to Yumei—Rong and Xia swaddled-borne following him several tens of thousands—self-titled Colonel Protecting the Western Qiang, Inspector of Yong, Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil struck in the Yongjia era he moved east to Yumei; tens of thousands of tribesmen and Chinese followed, and he styled himself colonel protecting the western Qiang, Yongzhou inspector, and Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 劉曜之平陳安也，以弋仲為平西將軍，封平襄公，邑之於隴上。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao pacified Chen An, he appointed Yizhong General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed Duke of Pingxiang, settled him on Longshang.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao crushed Chen An he named Yao Yizhong general who pacifies the west and Duke of Pingxiang with a fief on the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍克上邽，弋仲說之曰：「明公握兵十萬，功高一時，正是行權立策之日。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong overcame Shanggui, Yizhong persuaded him, saying: "Illustrious Lord grasps troops one hundred thousand—merit high one moment—this is exactly the day to wield power and set policy.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu took Shanggui, Yao Yizhong urged him, “You command a hundred thousand soldiers and stand supreme—now is the moment to seize initiative.”

sentences.zh: 隴上多豪，秦風猛勁，道隆後服，道洿先叛，宜徙隴上豪強，虛其心腹，以實畿甸。

translations.literal: Longshang abounds in magnates; Qin wind fierce strong—when the Way rises they submit late; when the Way sinks they rebel first—it is fitting to move Longshang magnates, empty their heart-belly, to fill the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi teems with strongmen whose Qin temperament turns volatile—relocate them from your heartland and settle them around the capital to strengthen the core.”

sentences.zh: 」季龍納之，啟勒以弋仲行安西將軍、六夷左都督。

translations.literal: " Jilong accepted it; reported to Le appointing Yizhong acting General Who Pacifies the West, Left Supervisor of the Six Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Hu agreed and had Shi Le appoint Yao Yizhong acting general who pacifies the west and left supervisor of the six tribes.

sentences.zh: 後晉豫州刺史祖約奔於勒，勒禮待之，弋仲上疏曰：「祖約殘賊晉朝，逼殺太后，不忠於主，而陛下寵之，臣恐奸亂之萌，此其始矣。

translations.literal: Later Jin Inspector of Yu Zu Yue fled to Le; Le courteously treated him; Yizhong submitted memorial saying: "Zu Yue cruelly injured Jin court—forced killed Empress Dowager—not loyal to lord—yet Your Majesty favors him—subject fears treacherous chaos's sprouting—this is its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s Yu governor Zu Yue fled to Shi Le, Yao Yizhong memorialized: “Zu Yue ravaged the court and slew the empress dowager—why honor him and sow sedition?”

sentences.zh: 」勒善之，後竟誅約。

translations.literal: " Le deemed it good; afterward ultimately executed Yue.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le agreed and later executed Zu Yue.

sentences.zh: 勒既死，季龍執權，思弋仲之言，遂徙秦、雍豪傑于關東。

translations.literal: After Le died, Jilong grasped power; pondered Yizhong's words; thereupon moved Qin and Yong heroes to east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Le died Shi Hu recalled Yao Yizhong’s counsel and resettled Qin and Yong magnates east of the passes.

sentences.zh: 弋仲率部眾數萬遷於清河，拜奮武將軍、西羌大都督，封襄平縣公。

translations.literal: Yizhong led departmental multitudes several tens of thousands moved to Qinghe; appointed General Who Rouses Might, Grand Supervisor of the Western Qiang, enfeoffed Duke of Xiangping county.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong led tens of thousands to Qinghe and received the titles general who rouses might, grand supervisor of the western Qiang, and Duke of Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 及季龍廢石弘自立，弋仲稱疾不賀。

translations.literal: When Jilong deposed Shi Hong and self-established, Yizhong claimed illness and did not congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu deposed Shi Hong and seized the throne Yao Yizhong feigned illness and skipped the court congratulation.

sentences.zh: 季龍累召之，乃赴，正色謂季龍曰：「奈何把臂受託而反奪之乎！

translations.literal: Jilong repeatedly summoned him; then he came; straight-faced said to Jilong: "How grasp arms receive entrustment yet turn seize it!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu summoned him repeatedly; Yao Yizhong came and demanded, “How can you clasp arms in trust and then steal the throne?”

sentences.zh: 」季龍憚其強正而不之責。

translations.literal: " Jilong feared his strong integrity and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Hu respected his blunt integrity and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 遷持節、十郡六夷大都督、冠軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Promoted Bearer of Staff, Grand Supervisor of Ten Commanderies Six Barbarians, Champion Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to staff-bearing grand supervisor over ten commanderies and six tribes and champion grand general.

sentences.zh: 性清儉鯁直，不修威儀，屢獻讜言，無所回避，季龍甚重之。

translations.literal: Nature pure frugal blunt straight—did not cultivate awe bearing—repeatedly presented frank words—nothing avoided—Jilong greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and blunt, heedless of pomp, he spoke plainly without flinching, and Shi Hu valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 朝之大議，靡不參決，公卿亦憚而推下之。

translations.literal: Court's great deliberations—none not participated in deciding—dukes and ministers also feared and yielded below him.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in on every great policy debate, and even senior ministers deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 武城左尉，季龍寵姬之弟也，曾擾其部，弋仲執尉，數以迫脅之狀，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: Wucheng Left Captain—Jilong's favored concubine's younger brother—once disturbed his department; Yizhong seized captain, enumerated coercion circumstance—ordered attendants behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The left captain of Wucheng, brother of Shi Hu’s favorite concubine, molested Yao Yizhong’s men; Yizhong seized him, listed his offenses, and had him decapitated.

sentences.zh: 尉叩頭流血，左右諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Captain knocked head bleeding—left and right remonstrated—then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The captain begged until blood ran; attendants pleaded and Yao Yizhong stayed the execution.

sentences.zh: 其剛直不回，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His rigid straightness not bending—all like this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such unbending integrity marked every incident.

sentences.zh: 季龍末，梁犢敗李農于滎陽，季龍大懼，馳召弋仲。

translations.literal: At Jilong's end, Liang Du defeated Li Nong at Xingyang—Jilong greatly feared—galloped summoning Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shi Hu’s reign Liang Du routed Li Nong at Xingyang; terrified, Shi Hu summoned Yao Yizhong in haste.

sentences.zh: 弋仲率其部眾八千餘人屯於南郊，輕騎至鄴。

translations.literal: Yizhong led his departmental multitudes more than eight thousand encamped at southern suburb—light cavalry arrived Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong camped eight thousand men south of Ye and rode lightly into the city.

sentences.zh: 時季龍病，不時見弋仲，引入領軍省，賜其所食之食。

translations.literal: At time Jilong ill—not timely seeing Yizhong—led into Army Lead Bureau—gifted his eaten food.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu was ill and delayed the audience, led him to the bureau of the commander of the guard, and offered him dinner.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒不食，曰：「召我擊賊，豈來覓食邪！

translations.literal: Yizhong angry did not eat—said: "Summoned me strike bandits—could it be come seeking food!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong refused food and snapped, “You called me to fight rebels—not to lunch!”

sentences.zh: 我不知上存亡，若一見，雖死無恨。

translations.literal: I do not know Sovereign's survival death—if once see—although die no regret.
translations.idiomatic: I know not whether our lord lives—grant one audience and I die content.”

sentences.zh: 」左右言之，乃引見。

translations.literal: " Attendants spoke it—thereupon led audience.
translations.idiomatic: ” His attendants relayed the plea and Shi Hu received him.

sentences.zh: 弋仲數季龍曰：「兒死來愁邪？

translations.literal: Yizhong reproached Jilong saying: "Son died come sorrow?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong scolded Shi Hu: “Do you sulk because your sons died?”

sentences.zh: 乃至於疾！

translations.literal: Even reach illness!
translations.idiomatic: Has grief brought you to this sickbed?”

sentences.zh: 兒小時不能使好人輔相，至令相殺。

translations.literal: Sons small-time could not employ good men assist—until ordering mutual killing.
translations.idiomatic: You never gave your boys worthy tutors, so they turned blades on each other.”

sentences.zh: 兒自有過，責其下人太甚，故反耳。

translations.literal: Sons themselves had faults—blamed their subordinates too extreme—therefore rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Your sons erred, yet you scourged their followers until revolt flared.”

sentences.zh: 汝病久，所立兒小，若不差，天下必亂。

translations.literal: You ill long—established son small—if not recover—under Heaven surely chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: You have lingered ill while the heir is a child—if you die the realm will boil.”

sentences.zh: 當宜憂此，不煩憂賊也。

translations.literal: Ought fitting worry this—not trouble worry bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Worry that, not Liang Du’s raiders.”

sentences.zh: 犢等因思歸之心，共為奸盜，所行殘賊，此成擒耳。

translations.literal: Du and others because homesick hearts—together acted treacherous banditry—what they did cruel banditry—this becomes capture ears.
translations.idiomatic: They are hungry bandits riding nostalgia—I will cage them in one blow.”

sentences.zh: 老羌請效死前鋒，使一舉而了。

translations.literal: Old Qiang requests offering death vanguard—enable one stroke and finish.
translations.idiomatic: Let this old Qiang die in your van and finish this.”

sentences.zh: 」弋仲性狷直，俗無尊卑皆汝之，季龍恕而不責，於坐授使持節、侍中、征西大將軍，賜以鎧馬。

translations.literal: " Yizhong nature blunt straight—custom without noble base all 'you' him—Jilong forgave and did not blame—at seat appointed Bearer of Staff, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West—gifted armor horse.
translations.idiomatic: ” Blunt to a fault, Yao Yizhong addressed everyone as “you”; Shi Hu laughed it off and at table invested him as staff-bearing palace attendant and general who conquers the west with armored horse.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「汝看老羌堪破賊以不？

translations.literal: Yizhong said: "You see old Qiang able destroy bandits or not?
translations.idiomatic: He asked, “Does this old Qiang look fit to break your rebels?”

sentences.zh: 」於是貫鉀跨馬於庭中，策馬南馳，不辭而出，遂滅梁犢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon threaded armor straddled horse in courtyard—whipped horse south galloped—without farewell went out—thereupon extinguished Liang Du.
translations.idiomatic: ” He armored up, vaulted his horse in the courtyard, galloped south without leave, and destroyed Liang Du.

sentences.zh: 以功加劍履上殿，入朝不趨，進封西平郡公。

translations.literal: By merit added sword shoes ascend hall—enter court not hasten—advanced enfeoff Duke of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he earned sword-and-shoes audience, leisure pace at court, and promotion to Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 冉閔之亂，弋仲率眾討閔，次於混橋。

translations.literal: Ran Min's chaos—Yizhong led multitudes attacking Min—halted at Hun Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: During Ran Min’s rising Yao Yizhong marched against him and camped at Hun Bridge.

sentences.zh: 石祗僭號于襄國，以弋仲為右丞相，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi arrogated title at Xiangguo—appointed Yizhong Right Chancellor—treated with special ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi declared himself emperor at Xiangguo, named Yao Yizhong right chancellor, and honored him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 祗與閔相攻，弋仲遣其子襄救祗，戒襄曰：「汝才十倍于閔，若不梟擒，不須復見我也。

translations.literal: Zhi and Min mutually attacked—Yizhong dispatched his son Xiang rescuing Zhi—warned Xiang saying: "Your talent tenfold Yu Min—if not owl-capture—need not again see me.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zhi and Ran Min clashed Yao Yizhong sent Yao Xiang to aid Shi Zhi with the vow: “You outmatch Ran Min tenfold—bring his head or do not return.”

sentences.zh: 」襄擊閔于常盧澤，大破之而歸。

translations.literal: " Xiang struck Min at Changlu Marsh—greatly defeated him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yao Xiang smashed Ran Min at Changlu Marsh but withdrew without capturing him.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒襄之不擒閔也，杖之一百。

translations.literal: Yizhong angry at Xiang's not capturing Min—caned him one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong flogged his son a hundred strokes for failing to seize Ran Min.

sentences.zh: 弋仲部曲馬何羅博學有文才，張豺之輔石世也，背弋仲歸豺，豺以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Yizhong retainer Ma Heluo broad learning had literary talent—when Zhang Chai assisted Shi Shi—betrayed Yizhong returning Chai—Chai appointed him Masters of Writing Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Heluo, Yao Yizhong’s follower, was learned and literary; when Zhang Chai sponsored Shi Shi he defected and Zhang made him a masters-of-writing gentleman.

sentences.zh: 豺敗，復歸，咸勸殺之。

translations.literal: Chai defeated—returned again—all urged killing him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Chai fell Ma returned; everyone urged execution.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「今正是招才納奇之日，當收其力用，不足害也。

translations.literal: Yizhong said: "Now is exactly summon talent admit marvel day—ought gather his strength use—not sufficient harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong said, “These are times to hoard talent—use his gifts; killing gains nothing.”

sentences.zh: 」以為參軍。

translations.literal: " Appointed Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: ” He named Ma army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 其寬恕如此。

translations.literal: His forgiveness like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 弋仲有子四十二人，常戒諸子曰：「吾本以晉室大亂，石氏待吾厚，故欲討其賊臣以報其德。

translations.literal: Yizhong had sons forty-two persons—often warned various sons saying: "I originally because Jin house great chaos—Shi house treated me thick—therefore wished attack their treacherous ministers to repay their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong had forty-two sons and often warned them: “When Jin collapsed the Shi treated us well, so I meant to punish their traitors in return.”

sentences.zh: 今石氏已滅，中原無主，自古以來未有戎狄作天子者。

translations.literal: Now Shi house already extinguished—Central Plain without lord—from antiquity until now never has Rong Di acted Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shi is gone and the heartland has no ruler—never has a tribesman sat as Son of Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 我死，汝便歸晉，當竭盡臣節，無為不義之事。

translations.literal: I die—you then return Jin—ought exhaust minister integrity—do not act unrighteous matters.
translations.idiomatic: When I die submit to Jin and serve with full loyalty—commit no injustice.”

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使請降。

translations.literal: " Thereupon dispatched envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent envoys to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 永和七年，拜弋仲使持節、六夷大都督、都督江、淮諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大單于，封高陵郡公。

translations.literal: Yonghe seventh year—appointed Yizhong Bearer of Staff, Grand Supervisor Six Barbarians, Supervisor Jiang Huai Military Affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, ceremonies equal Three Offices, Grand Chanyu—enfeoffed Duke of Gaoling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe seven (351) he received staff authority as grand supervisor of six tribes and Jiang-Huai armies, grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-duke honors, great chanyu, and Duke of Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: Eighth year—died—at time age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子襄之入關也，為苻生所敗，弋仲之柩為生所得，生以王禮葬之于天水冀縣。

translations.literal: When son Xiang entered Guan—was defeated by Fu Sheng—Yizhong's coffin was obtained by Sheng—Sheng with kingly ritual buried him at Tianshui Ji county.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xiang invaded Guanzhong Fu Sheng defeated him and seized Yao Yizhong’s coffin, burying it with princely honors at Ji in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 萇僭位，追諡曰景元皇帝，廟號始祖，墓曰高陵，置園邑五百家。

translations.literal: Chang arrogated throne—posthumously titled Emperor Jingyuan—temple name First Ancestor—tomb called Gaoling—established garden town five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang took the throne he posthumously honored him as Emperor Jingyuan, temple name First Ancestor, tomb Gaoling, with five hundred households to tend it.

sentences.zh: 襄字景國，弋仲之第五子也。

translations.literal: Xiang, courtesy name Jingguo—was Yizhong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang, courtesy name Jingguo, was Yao Yizhong’s fifth son.

sentences.zh: 年十七，身長八尺五寸，臂垂過膝，雄武多才藝，明察善撫納，士眾愛敬之，咸請為嗣。

translations.literal: Age seventeen—body length eight chi five cun—arms hung past knees—heroic martial many talents—clear discernment good at soothing accepting—soldiers beloved revered him—all requested as heir.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he stood eight chi five inches tall with arms past his knees, heroic and skilled, perceptive and winning loyalty; the army adored him and pressed him as heir.

sentences.zh: 弋仲弗許，百姓固請者日有千數，乃授之以兵。

translations.literal: Yizhong did not permit—the common people firmly requesting daily had thousand counts—thereupon entrusted him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong refused until thousands petitioned daily, then gave him command.

sentences.zh: 石祗僭號，以襄為使持節、驃騎將軍、護烏丸校尉、豫州刺史、新昌公。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi arrogated title—appointed Xiang Bearer of Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yu, Duke of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zhi claimed the throne he named Yao Xiang staff-bearing general of agile cavalry, colonel protecting the Wuhuan, Yu inspector, and Duke of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 晉遣使拜襄持節、平北將軍、并州刺史、即丘縣公。

translations.literal: Jin dispatched envoys appointing Xiang Bearer of Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing, Duke of Jiuqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: Jin invested him as general who pacifies the north, Bingzhou inspector, and Duke of Jiuqiu.

sentences.zh: 弋仲死，襄秘不發喪，率戶六萬南攻陽平、元城、發幹，皆破之，殺掠三千餘家，屯於碻磝津。

translations.literal: Yizhong died—Xiang secret did not issue mourning—led households sixty thousand south attacking Yangping, Yuancheng, Facan—all broke them—killed plundered more than three thousand households—encamped at Qiaoao Ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Yizhong died Yao Xiang hid the news, marched sixty thousand households south to storm Yangping, Yuancheng, and Facan, sacked three thousand families, and camped at Qiaoao ford.

sentences.zh: 以太原王亮為長史，天水尹赤為司馬，略陽伏子成為左部帥，南安斂岐為右部帥，略陽黑那為前部帥，強白為後部帥，太原薛贊、略陽王權翼為參軍。

translations.literal: Appointed Taiyuan Wang Liang Chief Clerk, Tianshui Yin Chi Major, Lueyang Fuzicheng Left Division Commander, Nan'an Lianqi Right Division Commander, Lueyang Heina Forward Division Commander, Qiangbai Rear Division Commander, Taiyuan Xue Zan, Lueyang Wang Quanyi Army Adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wang Liang chief clerk, Yin Chi major, Fuzicheng and Lianqi left and right division leaders, Heina and Qiangbai van and rear leaders, and Xue Zan and Wang Quanyi adjutants.

sentences.zh: 南至滎陽，始發喪行服。

translations.literal: South reached Xingyang—only then issued mourning wore garments.
translations.idiomatic: South of Xingyang he announced his father’s death and donned mourning.

sentences.zh: 與高昌、李曆戰于麻田，馬中流矢死，賴其弟萇以免。

translations.literal: With Gaochang, Li Li fought at Matian—horse mid-stream arrow died—relied on younger brother Chang to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Against Gaochang and Li Li at Matian his horse was shot; his brother Yao Chang saved him.

sentences.zh: 晉處襄於譙城，遣五弟為任，單騎度淮，見豫州刺史謝尚于壽春。

translations.literal: Jin situated Xiang at Qiaocheng—dispatched five younger brothers as hostage—single horse crossed Huai—saw Inspector of Yu Xie Shang at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin quartered him at Qiao with five brothers as hostages; he crossed the Huai alone to meet Yu governor Xie Shang at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 尚命去仗衛，幅巾以待之，一面交款，便若平生。

translations.literal: Shang ordered remove weapon guards—headcloth to await him—one meeting exchanged sincerity—then like whole life.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang dismissed guards and met him in casual dress; one meeting bred trust like old friends.

sentences.zh: 襄少有高名，雄武冠世，好學博通，雅善談論，英濟之稱著于南夏。

translations.literal: Xiang from youth had high name—heroic martial crowned age—loved learning broadly penetrated—elegant good discussion—heroic aid's title manifest in southern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned young for valor and arms, learned and eloquent, Yao Xiang was hailed across the south as a champion.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍、揚州刺史殷浩憚其威名，乃因襄諸弟，頻遣刺客殺襄，刺客皆推誠告實，襄待之若舊。

translations.literal: Central Army General, Inspector of Yang Yin Hao feared his awe name—thereupon via Xiang's various younger brothers—repeatedly dispatched assassins kill Xiang—assassins all pushed sincerity telling truth—Xiang treated them like old.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao feared him and sent killers through Yao Xiang’s brothers; each assassin confessed and Yao Xiang welcomed them like kin.

sentences.zh: 浩潛遣將軍魏憬率五千餘人襲襄，襄乃斬憬而並其眾。

translations.literal: Hao secretly dispatched General Wei Jing leading more than five thousand attacking Xiang—Xiang thereupon beheaded Jing and annexed his multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao secretly sent Wei Jing with five thousand men; Yao Xiang slew Wei Jing and absorbed his troops.

sentences.zh: 浩愈惡之，乃使將軍劉啟守譙，遷襄于梁國蠡台，表授梁國內史。

translations.literal: Hao increasingly hated him—thereupon ordered General Liu Qi guard Qiao—moved Xiang to Liang state's Litai—memorial appointed Liang interior steward.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao then garrisoned Liu Qi at Qiao, moved Yao Xiang to Litai in Liang, and named him interior steward of Liang.

sentences.zh: 襄遣權翼詣浩，浩曰：「姚平北每舉動自由，豈所望也。

translations.literal: Xiang dispatched Quanyi to Hao—Hao said: "Yao Pacifies-North each movement free—is this what hoped!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanyi called on Yin Hao, who said, “General Yao who pacifies the north acts as he pleases—hardly what we wished.”

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍輕納奸言，自生疑貳，愚謂猜嫌之由，不在於彼。

translations.literal: " Quanyi said: "General lightly accepted treacherous words—self-born suspicion twofold—foolish says suspicion's origin—not in them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Quanyi replied, “You credit slander and breed mistrust—the fault lies not with Yao Xiang.”

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「姚君縱放小人，盜竊吾馬，王臣之體固若是乎？

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Lord Yao indulged petty men—stole my horses—king minister's deportment indeed like this?
translations.idiomatic: ” Yin Hao said, “He lets underlings steal my horses—is that ministerial duty?”

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍謂姚平北以威武自強，終為難保，校兵練眾，將懲不恪，取馬者欲以自衛耳。

translations.literal: " Quanyi said: "General thinks Yao Pacifies-North by martial awe self-strengthens—ultimately hard protect—drill troops train multitudes—about to punish not reverent—horse-takers wished to self-defend ears.
translations.idiomatic: ” Quanyi answered, “You fear his army and drill your own; he took horses only to guard himself.”

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「何至是也。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "How reach this!
translations.idiomatic: ” Yin Hao said, “Surely not.”

sentences.zh: 」浩遣謝萬討襄，襄逆擊破之。

translations.literal: " Hao dispatched Xie Wan attacking Xiang—Xiang counter-struck defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yin Hao sent Xie Wan; Yao Xiang routed him.

sentences.zh: 浩甚怒，會聞關中有變，浩率眾北伐，襄乃要擊浩于山桑，大敗之，斬獲萬計，收其資仗。

translations.literal: Hao greatly angry—happened hear Guanzhong had change—Hao led multitudes north campaign—Xiang then intercepted Hao at Shansang—greatly defeated him—beheaded captured counted by tens of thousands—seized his supplies weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Yin Hao marched north on Guanzhong news; Yao Xiang ambushed him at Shansang, slaughtered thousands, and seized baggage and arms.

sentences.zh: 使兄益守山桑壘，復如淮南。

translations.literal: Ordered elder brother Yi guard Shansang rampart—again went Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He left his brother Yi at Shansang and returned to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 浩遣劉啟、王彬之伐山桑，襄自淮南擊滅之，鼓行濟淮，屯於盱眙，招掠流人，眾至七萬，分置守宰，勸課農桑，遣使建鄴，罪狀殷浩，並自陳謝。

translations.literal: Hao dispatched Liu Qi, Wang Binzhi attacking Shansang—Xiang from Huainan struck extinguished them—drum marched crossed Huai—encamped at Xuyi—summoned plundered wandering people—multitudes reached seventy thousand—distributed set guards stewards—urged agriculture mulberry—dispatched envoys Jianye—accused Yin Hao—and self explained apology.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao sent Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi, Yao Xiang destroyed them from Huainan, crossed the Huai to Xuyi with seventy thousand followers, organized officials, promoted farming, and wrote to Jianye denouncing Yin Hao while apologizing for himself.

sentences.zh: 流人郭斁等千餘人執晉堂邑內史劉仕降於襄，朝延大震，以吏部尚書周閔為中軍將軍，緣江備守。

translations.literal: Wanderers Guo Yi and others more than thousand seized Jin Tangyi interior steward Liu Shi surrendering to Xiang—court extended greatly shook—appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min Central Army General—along Yang prepared defense.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand refugees led by Guo Yi seized Liu Shi and yielded to Yao Xiang; the court trembled and named Zhou Min central army general to guard the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 襄將佐部眾皆北人，咸勸襄北還。

translations.literal: Xiang's generals aides multitudes all northern men—all urged Xiang north return.
translations.idiomatic: His northern officers urged him to march north.

sentences.zh: 襄方軌北引，自稱大將軍、大單于，進攻外黃，為晉邊將所敗。

translations.literal: Xiang parallel-tracks north led—self-titled Grand General, Grand Chanyu—advanced attacking Waihuang—was defeated by Jin border generals.
translations.idiomatic: He drove north as grand general and great chanyu, attacked Waihuang, and lost to Jin frontier forces.

sentences.zh: 襄收散卒而勤撫恤之，於是復振。

translations.literal: Xiang gathered scattered soldiers and diligently soothed them—thereupon again revived.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the fugitives with care and restored morale.

sentences.zh: 乃據許昌，將如河東以圖關右，自許遂攻洛陽，逾月不克。

translations.literal: Thereupon occupied Xuchang—about to go Hedong to plot Guan right—from Xu then attacked Luoyang—passed month did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: He held Xuchang, planned Hedong and the northwest, then struck Luoyang from Xu without taking it in a month.

sentences.zh: 其長史王亮諫襄曰：「公英略蓋天下，士眾思效力命，不可損威勞眾，守此孤城。

translations.literal: His Chief Clerk Wang Liang remonstrated Xiang saying: "Lord's heroic strategy caps under Heaven—soldiers desire offer strength life—cannot harm awe tire multitudes—guard this lone city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang urged, “Your genius fills the realm and men yearn to serve—do not waste strength on this lonely city.”

sentences.zh: 宜還河北，以弘遠略。

translations.literal: It is fitting return Hebei—to expand far strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Return north of the Yellow River and pursue the larger design.”

sentences.zh: 」襄曰：「洛陽雖小，山河四塞之固，亦是用武之地。

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "Luoyang although small—mountains rivers four barriers' solidity—is also terrain of military use.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yao Xiang replied, “Luoyang is small yet fortified by mountains and rivers—a worthy base.”

sentences.zh: 吾欲先據洛陽，然後開建大業。

translations.literal: I wish first occupy Luoyang—afterward open establish great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to take Luoyang first, then raise the great enterprise.”

sentences.zh: 」俄而亮卒，襄哭之甚慟，曰：「天將不欲成吾事乎？

translations.literal: " Soon Liang died—Xiang wept for him greatly mournful—said: "Heaven about not wish complete my affairs?
translations.idiomatic: ” When Wang Liang died soon after, Yao Xiang wailed, “Does heaven forbid my success?”

sentences.zh: 王亮舍我去也！」

translations.literal: Wang Liang abandoned me departed!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang has left me!”

sentences.zh: 晉征西大將軍桓溫自江陵伐襄，戰于伊水北，為溫所敗，率麾下數千騎奔於北山。

translations.literal: Jin General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen from Jiangling attacked Xiang—fought north of Yi River—was defeated by Wen—led under-flag several thousand cavalry fled to North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen marched from Jianglang, defeated Yao Xiang north of the Yi, who fled into the northern hills with thousands of horse.

sentences.zh: 其夜，百姓棄妻子隨襄者五千餘人，屯據陽鄉，赴者又四千餘戶。

translations.literal: That night common people abandoned wives children following Xiang were more than five thousand—encamped occupying Yangxiang—who came were again more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: That night over five thousand civilians forsook families to follow him at Yangxiang; four thousand more households joined.

sentences.zh: 襄前後敗喪數矣，眾知襄所在，輒扶老攜幼賓士而赴之。

translations.literal: Xiang front back defeat loss several times—multitude knowing Xiang's whereabouts—always supporting old carrying young as guests knights hastened to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though often beaten, wherever Yao Xiang went throngs carried elders and children to join him.

sentences.zh: 時或傳襄創重不濟，溫軍所得士女莫不北望揮涕。

translations.literal: Sometimes word spread that Xiang's wound was grave and he would not survive; among the men and women taken by Wen's army none failed to look north and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors flew that Yao Xiang's wounds were mortal; every captive Huan Wen's army had seized turned north and shed tears.

sentences.zh: 其得物情如此。

translations.literal: Thus did he win the sentiment of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the devotion he commanded among the people.

sentences.zh: 先是，弘農楊亮歸襄，襄待以客禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had joined Xiang; Xiang treated him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had come over to Yao Xiang, who received him with full guest honors.

sentences.zh: 後奔桓溫，溫問襄於亮，亮曰：「神明器宇，孫策之儔，而雄武過之。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Huan Wen; Wen asked Liang about Xiang. Liang said: "He has spirit-like bearing and presence—the peer of Sun Ce—and in heroic martial prowess surpasses him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang later crossed to Huan Wen, who pressed him about Yao Xiang. Liang answered: "He carries himself like a god among men—Sun Ce's equal—and exceeds him in bold warcraft.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如是。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which others held him.

sentences.zh: 萇字景茂，弋仲第二十四子也。

translations.literal: Chang styled Jingmao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, courtesy name Jingmao, was Yao Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.

sentences.zh: 少聰哲，多權略，廓落任率，不修行業，諸兄皆奇之。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and discerning, rich in stratagem, broad-minded and forthright; he did not cultivate conventional conduct—his elder brothers all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and resourceful from boyhood, openhanded and blunt, he spurned petty propriety, and his brothers wondered at him.

sentences.zh: 隨襄征伐，每參大謀。

translations.literal: He followed Xiang on campaign and took part in every major plan.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with Yao Xiang on campaign and shared in each great decision.

sentences.zh: 襄之寇洛陽也，夢萇服袞衣，升御坐，諸酋長皆侍立，旦謂將佐曰：「吾夢如此，此兒志度不恆，或能大起吾族。

translations.literal: When Xiang raided Luoyang, he dreamed that Chang wore ceremonial robes, ascended the imperial seat, and all chieftains stood in attendance; at dawn he told his officers: "I have dreamed thus—this boy's ambition is not ordinary—perhaps he can greatly exalt our clan.
translations.idiomatic: During Yao Xiang's thrust on Luoyang he dreamed Yao Chang robed as emperor on the throne while tribal headmen stood attendance. At dawn he told his staff: "That dream tells me this son's aims are no common thing—maybe he will lift our house high.

sentences.zh: 」襄之敗于麻田也，馬中流矢死，萇下馬以授襄，襄曰：「汝何以自免？

translations.literal: At Xiang's defeat at Matian his horse was struck mid-gallop and died; Chang dismounted and gave his mount to Xiang. Xiang said: "How then will you save yourself?
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xiang lost at Matian, his horse fell to an arrow; Yao Chang sprang down and handed him his own. Xiang asked, "How will you escape?

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「但令兄濟，豎子安敢害萇！

translations.literal: Chang said: "Only let elder brother reach safety—what stripling would dare harm Chang!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang replied: "Once you are safe, what fool would dare touch me!

sentences.zh: 」會救至，俱免。

translations.literal: Relief arrived in time; both were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Help rode up and both men survived.

sentences.zh: 及襄死，萇率諸弟降于苻生。

translations.literal: When Xiang died, Chang led his younger brothers to surrender to Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Xiang fell, Yao Chang brought his brothers to submit to Fu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 苻堅以萇為揚武將軍。

translations.literal: Fu Jian appointed Chang General Who Raises Might.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian named him General Who Raises Might.

sentences.zh: 曆左衛將軍，隴東、汲郡、河東、武都、武威、巴西、扶風太守，甯、幽、兗三州刺史，復為揚武將軍，步兵校尉，封益都侯。

translations.literal: He successively served as General of the Left Guard, Administrator of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Ba-xi, and Fufeng; Inspector of the three provinces Ning, You, and Yan; again as General Who Raises Might and Colonel of Foot Soldiers; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Left Guard general; governed Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Ba-xi, and Fufeng; held Ning, You, and Yanzhou; returned to General Who Raises Might and colonel of foot; and received the marquisate of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 為堅將，累有大功。

translations.literal: As Jian's general he repeatedly earned great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 初，萇隨楊安伐蜀，嘗晝寢水旁，上有神光煥然，左右咸異之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang followed Yang An to attack Shu, he once napped by day beside the water; divine light blazed above him, and those around him all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while serving under Yang An in the Shu campaign, he slept by a stream at noon; a supernatural radiance played overhead, and his companions took it for an omen.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅寇晉，以萇為龍驤將軍、督益、梁州諸軍事，謂萇曰：「朕本以龍驤建業，龍驤之號未曾假人，今特以相授，山南之事一以委卿。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian invaded Jin he appointed Chang Dragon-General and supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Liang prefectures, saying to him: "I originally founded the enterprise as Dragon-General; the Dragon-General title has never been lent to another—now I grant it especially to you—affairs south of the mountains I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jin invasion Fu Jian made Yao Chang Dragon-General and area commander for Yi and Liang. He told him: "I began my rise under that banner and have never given the title away—now it is yours. Everything south of the Qinling is in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」堅左將軍竇沖進曰：「王者無戲言，此將不祥之征也，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: Jian's Left General Dou Chong advanced and said: "A king has no jesting words—this generalship is an ill omen—may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Left general Dou Chong objected: "Rulers do not speak in sport—that commission is a dark portent; please reconsider, Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」堅默然。

translations.literal: Jian was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said nothing.

sentences.zh: 堅既敗於淮南，歸長安，慕容泓起兵叛堅。

translations.literal: After Jian was defeated at Huainan he returned to Chang'an; Murong Hong raised troops and rebelled against Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten at Huainan, Fu Jian withdrew to Chang'an as Murong Hong rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 堅遣子叡討之，以萇為司馬。

translations.literal: Jian sent his son Rui to punish him and appointed Chang marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian dispatched his son Fu Rui against Hong and named Yao Chang his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 為泓所敗，叡死之。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Hong; Rui died.
translations.idiomatic: Hong broke them and Fu Rui was killed.

sentences.zh: 萇遣龍驤長史趙都詣堅謝罪，堅怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Chang sent Dragon-General Senior Clerk Zhao Du to Jian to apologize; Jian was angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent his Dragon-General chief clerk Zhao Du to apologize; Fu Jian in fury executed him.

sentences.zh: 萇懼，奔於渭北，遂如馬牧。

translations.literal: Chang feared and fled to the north of the Wei; then he went to the horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yao Chang bolted across the Wei to the northern pasturelands.

sentences.zh: 西州豪族尹詳、趙曜、王欽盧、王欽盧、牛雙、狄廣、張乾等率五萬餘家，咸推萇為盟主。

translations.literal: Magnate clans of the western march—Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu, Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian, and others—led more than fifty thousand households and together elevated Chang as covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: Western magnates Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu, Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian, and others—over fifty thousand households—united to make Yao Chang their league chief.

sentences.zh: 萇將距之，天水尹緯說萇曰：「今百六之數既臻，秦亡之兆已見，以將軍威靈命世，必能匡濟時艱，故豪傑驅馳，咸同推仰。

translations.literal: Chang was about to refuse them when Yin Wei of Tianshui persuaded him: "Now the cycle of ruin has arrived and omens of Qin's fall are plain; by the general's august mandate he can surely rescue the age from hardship—therefore heroes gallop in and alike push you upward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang meant to decline until Yin Wei of Tianshui urged him: "The fatal cycle has turned; Qin's end is written. Your prestige fits the hour—you alone can right this ruin—so every bold spirit rallies and lifts you.

sentences.zh: 明公宜降心從議，以副群望，不可坐觀沈溺而不拯救之。

translations.literal: Illustrious Lord ought to humble his heart and heed counsel—to match the multitude's hopes—you cannot sit and watch men sink and drown without rescuing them.
translations.idiomatic: Humble yourself to their counsel and answer what the realm expects—do not watch the world drown from the shore.

sentences.zh: 」萇乃從緯謀，乙太元九年自稱大將軍、大單于、萬年秦王，大赦境內，年號白雀，稱制行事。

translations.literal: Chang then followed Wei's plan; in Taiyuan ninth year he styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, Prince of Wannian Qin; proclaimed a general amnesty within his borders; era name White Sparrow; exercised imperial authority and conducted affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang took Wei's advice. In Taiyuan 384 he proclaimed himself grand general, great chanyu, and prince of Qin at Wannian; ordered a realm-wide amnesty, adopted the reign title White Sparrow, and issued orders as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 以天水尹詳、南安龐演為左右長史，南安姚晃、尹緯為左右司馬，天水狄伯支、焦虔、梁希、龐魏、任謙為從事中郎，姜訓、閻遵為掾屬，王據、焦世、蔣秀、尹延年、牛雙、張乾為參軍，王欽盧、姚方成、王破虜、楊難、尹嵩、裴騎、趙曜、狄廣、黨刪等為帥。

translations.literal: He appointed Yin Xiang of Tianshui and Pang Yan of Nan'an as left and right senior clerks; Yao Huang of Nan'an and Yin Wei as left and right masters of records; Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, and Ren Qian of Tianshui as consultant gentlemen; Jiang Xun and Yan Zun as staff clerks; Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian as adjutants; and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan, and others as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yin Xiang and Pang Yan senior clerks left and right; Yao Huang and Yin Wei masters of records; Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, and Ren Qian consultant gentlemen; Jiang Xun and Yan Zun staff officers; Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian adjutants; and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan, and others as column commanders.

sentences.zh: 時慕容沖與苻堅相攻，眾甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time Murong Chong and Fu Jian attacked each other; Chong's host was very large.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong and Fu Jian were locked in battle, and Chong's army swelled.

sentences.zh: 萇將西上，恐沖遏之，乃遣使通和，以子崇為質於沖，進屯北地，厲兵積粟，以觀時變。

translations.literal: Chang was about to march west and feared Chong would block him; he therefore sent envoys to negotiate peace and gave his son Chong as hostage to Chong; advanced and encamped at Beidi; sharpened weapons and stored grain—to watch the times' changes.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching west Yao Chang feared Murong Chong might bar his path, so he sued for peace and left his son Yao Chong as hostage; he camped at Beidi, drilled troops, stockpiled grain, and waited on events.

sentences.zh: 苻堅先徙晉人李祥等數千戶于敷陸，至是，降於萇，北地、新平、安定羌胡降者十餘萬戶。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had earlier relocated several thousand households of Jin people such as Li Xiang to Fulu; at this time they surrendered to Chang; of Qiang and Hu who surrendered in Beidi, Xinping, and Anding there were more than a hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian had moved thousands of Jin households such as Li Xiang's to Fulu; they now came over to Yao Chang, and more than a hundred thousand Qiang and Hu households in Beidi, Xinping, and Anding followed suit.

sentences.zh: 堅率諸將攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: Jian led his generals to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian threw his generals at Yao Chang but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 萇聞容慕沖攻長安，議進趨之計，群下咸曰：「宜先據咸陽以制天下。

translations.literal: When Chang heard Rong Mu Chong attack Chang'an, he debated plans for advancing; his subordinates all said: "It is fitting first to seize Xianyang and thereby control All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Murong Chong was closing on Chang'an; Yao Chang's council urged him: "Take Xianyang first and you command the realm.

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「燕因懷舊之士而起兵，若功成事捷，咸有東歸之思，安能久固秦川！

translations.literal: Chang said: "Yan raised troops thanks to men homesick for old Yan—if merit is achieved and affairs succeed swiftly, all will harbor thoughts of returning east—how can they long secure the Qin riverlands!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang disagreed: "The Yan host fights for old homes—once they win they will stream eastward; they cannot hold the Guanzhong basin for long.

sentences.zh: 吾欲移兵嶺北，廣收資實，須秦弊燕回，然後垂拱取之。

translations.literal: I desire to shift troops north of the ridges, broadly gather supplies and assets, wait until Qin is exhausted and Yan withdraws—then with draped sleeves take it.
translations.idiomatic: I will shift north of the mountains, hoard grain and gear, and wait until Qin is spent and Yan retreats—then take the prize without lifting a blade.

sentences.zh: 兵不血刃，坐定天下，此卞莊得二之義也。

translations.literal: Weapons without blood on blades—sit and settle All-under-Heaven—this is the meaning of Bian Zhuang catching two.
translations.idiomatic: No blood on the sword yet the empire settled—the stratagem of Bian Zhuang letting two tigers wound each other.

sentences.zh: 」堅甯朔將軍宋方率騎三千從雲中將赴長安，萇自貳縣要破之，方單馬奔免，其司馬田晃率眾降萇。

translations.literal: Jian's General Who Pacifies the North Song Fang led three thousand cavalry from Yunzhong bound for Chang'an; Chang intercepted him from Er county and defeated him; Fang alone on horseback fled and escaped; his marshal Tian Huang led the host to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's northern general Song Fang rode three thousand horsemen from Yunzhong toward Chang'an; Yao Chang ambushed him at Er county and broke his column. Fang escaped alone; his chief of staff Tian Huang brought the remainder to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 萇遣諸將攻新平，克之，因略地至安定，嶺北諸城盡降之。

translations.literal: Chang sent generals to attack Xinping and overcame it; thereupon raided territory as far as Anding; all cities north of the ridges wholly surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang stormed Xinping, swept on toward Anding, and every walled town north of the Qinling opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅為慕容沖所逼，走入五將山。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Jian was pressed by Murong Chong and fled into Mount Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong drove Fu Jian from the field; the emperor fled into the Wujiang hills.

sentences.zh: 沖入長安。

translations.literal: Chong entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong seized Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 堅司隸校尉權翼、尚書趙遷、大鴻臚皇甫覆、光祿大夫薛贊、扶風太守段鏗等文武數百人奔於萇。

translations.literal: Jian's Metropolitan Governor Quan Yi, Masters of Writing Zhao Qian, Grand Herald Huangfu Fu, Grand Counselor Xue Zan, Administrator of Fufeng Duan Keng, and several hundred civil and military men fled to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Fu Jian's officials—among them Metropolitan Governor Quan Yi, Secretary Zhao Qian, Grand Herald Huangfu Fu, Privy Counselor Xue Zan, and Fufeng governor Duan Keng—defected to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 萇遣驍騎將軍吳忠率騎圍堅，萇如新平。

translations.literal: Chang sent Valiant Cavalry General Wu Zhong to lead cavalry and surround Jian; Chang went to Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang ordered Valiant Cavalry general Wu Zhong to pin Fu Jian with cavalry while he himself struck toward Xinping.

sentences.zh: 俄而忠執堅，送之。

translations.literal: Soon Zhong seized Jian and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Wu Zhong took Fu Jian captive and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖遣其車騎大將軍高蓋率眾五萬來伐，戰于新平南，大破之，蓋率麾下數千人來降，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Murong Chong sent his General of Chariots and Cavalry Gao Gai leading fifty thousand troops to campaign against him; they fought south of Xinping; Chang greatly defeated them; Gai led several thousand under his command to come surrender; Chang appointed him Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong sent chariot-and-cavalry commander Gao Gai at Yao Chang with fifty thousand men; south of Xinping Yao Chang shattered the column. Gai crossed over with thousands of survivors and received appointment as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 沖既率眾東下，長安空虛。

translations.literal: Once Chong had led the host east downward, Chang'an was empty and hollow.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chong marched east, Chang'an lay open.

sentences.zh: 盧水郝奴稱帝于長安，渭北盡應之。

translations.literal: Hao Nu of the Lu River styled himself emperor at Chang'an; north of the Wei all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Nu of the Lu-shui tribes proclaimed himself emperor at Chang'an, and the north bank of the Wei rose with him.

sentences.zh: 扶風王驎有眾數千，保據馬嵬。

translations.literal: Wang Lin of Fufeng had several thousand followers and held Mawei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin of Fufeng mustered a few thousand men and held the Mawei defile.

sentences.zh: 奴遣弟多攻驎。

translations.literal: Nu sent younger brother Duo to attack Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Nu sent his brother Hao Duo against Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 萇伐驎，破之，驎走漢中。

translations.literal: Chang attacked Lin, defeated him, and Lin fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang struck Wang Lin, broke his force, and Lin fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 執多而進攻奴，降之。

translations.literal: He seized Duo and advanced to attack Nu and made him surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He took Duo captive, pressed on against Hao Nu, and forced his surrender.

sentences.zh: 乙太元十一年萇僭即皇帝位於長安，大赦，改元曰建初，國號大秦，改長安曰常安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taiyuan, Chang unlawfully assumed the emperor's seat at Chang'an, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianchu, declared the state name Great Qin, and renamed Chang'an to Chang'an (Everlasting Peace).
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 386, Yao Chang seized the throne at Chang'an in open usurpation: he declared an amnesty, adopted the reign title Jianchu, named his state Great Qin, and rechristened the capital Chang'an as Everlasting Peace.

sentences.zh: 立妻虵氏為皇后，子興為皇太子，置百官。

translations.literal: He established his wife of the She clan as empress, his son Xing as crown prince, and appointed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Lady She to empress, named his son Yao Xing crown prince, and filled out the imperial bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 自謂以火德承苻氏木行，服色如漢氏承周故事。

translations.literal: He claimed that by the virtue of Fire he succeeded the Fu clan's Wood phase, and that vestments and colors followed the Han precedent of succeeding Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He declared that Fire succeeded the Fu house's Wood in the cycle of virtues, and dressed his court after the Han model's succession from Zhou.

sentences.zh: 徙安定五千餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: He relocated more than five thousand households from Anding to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled over five thousand Anding households to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以弟征虜緒為司隸校尉，鎮長安。

translations.literal: He appointed his younger brother Zheng-lü Xu Metropolitan Governor and garrisoned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his brother Yao Xu—General Who Subdues the Enemy—the post of Metropolitan Governor and left him to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 萇如安定，擊平涼胡金熙、鮮卑沒奕於，大破之。

translations.literal: Chang went to Anding, attacked the Pingliang Hu Jin Xi and the Xianbei Moyuyu, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang marched to Anding, fell upon Jin Xi of the Pingliang Hu and Moyuyu of the Xianbei, and shattered both hosts.

sentences.zh: 遂如秦州，與苻堅秦州刺史王統相持，天水屠各、略陽羌胡應萇者二萬餘戶，統懼，乃降。

translations.literal: He then went to Qinzhou and was locked in stalemate with Wang Tong, Fu Jian's Inspector of Qinzhou; more than twenty thousand households of Tuge from Tianshui and Qiang and Hu from Lüeyang who responded to Chang—Tong feared and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed into Qinzhou, where he and Wang Tong—Fu Jian's inspector—glared at each other across the lines. When more than twenty thousand Tianshui Tuge and Lüeyang Qiang and Hu households rallied to Yao Chang, Tong lost heart and yielded.

sentences.zh: 因饗將士於上邽，南安人古成詵進曰：「臣州人殷地險，俊傑如林，用武之國也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feasted officers and soldiers at Shanggui, and Gu Cheng Shen of Nan'an stepped forward and said, "My province is populous and its land perilous; outstanding men stand thick as a forest—it is a state for wielding arms.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanggui he feasted his troops. Gu Cheng Shen of Nan'an came forward: "This land is crowded with people and folded in rough terrain; talent clusters here like trees in a forest—it was made for war."

sentences.zh: 王秦州不能收拔賢才，三分鼎足，而坐玩珠玉，以至於此。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Qinzhou could not gather and elevate worthy men, could not maintain a third of the tripod, but sat playing with pearls and jade, and came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Your predecessor could neither gather good men nor hold his third of the realm; he sat fondling gems until everything collapsed.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜散秦州金帛以施六軍，旌賢表善以副鄙州之望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to disperse Qinzhou's gold and silk to supply the Six Armies, and mark out the worthy and display the good to match the hopes of this humble province."
translations.idiomatic: Spend Qinzhou's gold and silk on the armies; honor the worthy and lift up the virtuous—give this province what it has been waiting for.

sentences.zh: 」萇善之，擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Chang approved of it and promoted him to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang approved and raised Shen to Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拜弟碩德都督隴右諸軍事、征西將軍、秦州刺史，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: He appointed his younger brother Shuode Supervisor of Military Affairs for Longyou, General Who Conquers the West, Inspector of Qinzhou, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and garrisoned Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He named his brother Yao Shuode commander on the Longyou front, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Qinzhou, with the Eastern Qiang commission, and stationed him at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 萇還安定，修德政，布惠化，省非急之費，以救時弊，閭閻之士有豪介之善者，皆顯異之。

translations.literal: Chang returned to Anding, cultivated virtuous government, spread benevolent transformation, reduced expenditures that were not urgent to remedy the ills of the times; among commoners who had heroic-uprightness goodness, he all displayed and distinguished them.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Anding, Yao Chang pursued humane rule and generous policies, cut every expense that could wait, and tried to heal a broken age; commoners of stubborn integrity he singled out for honor.

sentences.zh: 萇復如秦州，為苻登所敗，語在《登傳》。

translations.literal: Chang again went to Qinzhou and was defeated by Fu Deng; the words are in the "Deng" biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang returned to Qinzhou and lost to Fu Deng; the full account is in Deng's memoir.

sentences.zh: 以其太子興鎮長安，而與登相距。

translations.literal: He used his crown prince Xing to garrison Chang'an and opposed Deng at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He left Crown Prince Yao Xing to hold Chang'an while he kept Fu Deng at bay.

sentences.zh: 登馮翊太守蘭犢與苻師奴離貳，慕容永攻之，犢遣使請救。

translations.literal: Deng's Administrator of Fengyi Lan Du and Fu Shinu were at odds; Murong Yong attacked him; Du sent envoys begging rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's Fengyi governor Lan Du had broken with Fu Shinu; Murong Yong struck Du, who sent envoys pleading for aid.

sentences.zh: 萇將赴救，尚書令姚旻、左僕射尹緯等言於萇曰：「苻登近在瓦亭，陛下未宜輕舉。

translations.literal: Chang was about to go to the rescue when Grand Secretary Yao Min, Left Vice Director Yin Wei, and others spoke to Chang, saying, "Fu Deng is near at Wuting; Your Majesty ought not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang was riding to the rescue when Grand Secretary Yao Min, Yin Wei the Left Vice Director, and others warned him: "Fu Deng sits at Wuting—too close for you to march rashly."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「登遲重少決，每失時機，聞吾自行，正當廣集兵資，必不能輕軍深入。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Deng is sluggish-heavy and seldom decisive; always misses the opportunity; hearing that I go myself, he will only broadly gather troops and supplies—he cannot with a light army go deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang replied: "Deng is slow and seldom commits; he habitually misses the hour. News that I lead in person will send him scrambling to hoard men and grain—he will not dare a fast, shallow thrust."

sentences.zh: 兩月之間，足可克此三豎，吾事必矣。

translations.literal: Within two months it is enough to overcome these three striplings; my affair is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Two months will suffice to break those three whelps—and then my work is done.

sentences.zh: 」遂師次於渥源。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army encamped at Woyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The host halted at Woyuan.

sentences.zh: 師奴率眾來距，大戰，敗之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Shinu led the host to oppose; great battle; defeated him; wholly captured his host.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shinu advanced to meet him. After a pitched battle Yao Chang broke him and took every man captive.

sentences.zh: 又擒蘭犢，收其士馬。

translations.literal: He also seized Lan Du and collected his soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Lan Du as well and rounded up his troops and mounts.

sentences.zh: 萇乃掘苻堅屍，鞭撻無數，裸剝衣裳，薦之以棘，坎土而埋之。

translations.literal: Chang then dug up Fu Jian's corpse, flogged it countless times, stripped naked the clothing, spread thorns under him, and buried him with earth in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang had Fu Jian's body exhumed, lashed it beyond counting, stripped it bare, heaped brambles beneath the corpse, and shoveled it into a pit.

sentences.zh: 慕容永征西將軍王宣率眾降萇。

translations.literal: Murong Yong's General Who Conquers the West Wang Xuan led the host to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan—Murong Yong's general on the western front—brought his command over to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 初，關西雄傑以苻氏既終，萇雄略命世，天下之事可一旦而定。

translations.literal: At first the champions west of the Pass thought the Fu clan had already ended and Chang's heroic stratagems commanded the age; the affairs of All-under-Heaven could be settled in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Once, the strongmen beyond the Pass believed the Fu house finished and Yao Chang unrivaled in daring—surely the empire could be settled before noon.

sentences.zh: 萇既與苻登相持積年，數為登所敗，遠近咸懷去就之計，唯征虜齊難、冠軍徐洛生、輔國劉郭單、冠威彌姐婆觸、龍驤趙惡地、鎮北梁國兒等守忠不貳，並留子弟守營，供繼軍糧，身將精卒，隨萇征伐。

translations.literal: Once Chang had been locked in stalemate with Fu Deng for accumulated years and repeatedly was defeated by Deng, far and near all harbored plans of going or staying—only Zheng-lü Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Fu-guo Liu Guoshan, Guan-wei Mizijie Pochu, Dragon-General Zhao Edui, Zhen-bei Liang Guo'er, and the like guarded loyalty without twofoldness; together they left sons and younger brothers to guard camps, supplied successive army grain, themselves led crack soldiers, and followed Chang in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Years of deadlock with Fu Deng—and repeated defeats—left allies everywhere weighing whether to stay or bolt. Only Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guoshan, Mizijie Pochu, Zhao Edui, Liang Guo'er, and a handful like them stayed true: they left kin to guard the camps, kept grain flowing to the army, and rode with picked troops at Yao Chang's side.

sentences.zh: 時諸營既多，故號萇軍為大營，大營之號自此始也。

translations.literal: At the time the various camps were already many; therefore Chang's army was titled Great Camp; the title Great Camp begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: So many camps had sprung up that men began calling Yao Chang's host the Great Camp—the name starts here.

sentences.zh: 時天大雪，萇下書深自責罰，散後宮文綺珍寶以供戎事，身食一味，妻不重彩。

translations.literal: At the time heaven greatly snowed; Chang issued a document deeply blaming himself, dispersed the rear palace's patterned silks and treasures to supply military affairs, personally ate one flavor, wives did not heavy colors.
translations.idiomatic: Snow poured from the sky. Yao Chang issued a self-rebuke in writing, poured the harem's silks and jewels into the war effort, ate a single dish at each meal, and forbade his consorts bright robes.

sentences.zh: 將帥死王事者，加秩二等，士卒戰沒，皆有褒贈。

translations.literal: Commanders and generals who died on king business had ranks raised two grades; soldiers killed in battle all had commendation gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who died in service rose two ranks posthumously; every soldier fallen in battle received honors and stipends for his kin.

sentences.zh: 立太學，禮先賢之後。

translations.literal: He established the Imperial Academy and treated with ritual the descendants of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Imperial Academy and received the descendants of ancient sages with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 敦煌索盧曜請刺苻登，萇曰：「卿以身徇難，將為誰乎？

translations.literal: Dunhuang Suolu Yao requested to assassinate Fu Deng; Chang said, "You with body follow hardship—for whom will it be?
translations.idiomatic: Suolu Yao of Dunhuang volunteered to slip a blade into Fu Deng. Yao Chang asked, "You mean to die for this—whose victory would that buy?"

sentences.zh: 」曜曰：「臣死之後，深以友人隴西辛暹仰托。

translations.literal: Yao said, "After I die, deeply I entrust upward to my friend Xin Xian of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao answered, "When I am gone, look after my friend Xin Xian of Longxi—that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 」萇遣之。

translations.literal: Chang dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang let him go.

sentences.zh: 事發，為登所殺，萇以暹為騎都尉。

translations.literal: The affair erupted; he was killed by Deng; Chang appointed Xian Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The plot surfaced; Deng executed Suolu Yao; Yao Chang named Xin Xian Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 登進逼安定，諸將勸萇決戰，萇曰：「與窮寇競勝，兵家之下。

translations.literal: Deng advanced pressing Anding; the generals urged Chang to decisive battle; Chang said, "With an exhausted bandit competing victory is of the lowest in the art of war.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng pressed toward Anding; his captains begged for a pitched battle. Yao Chang refused to oblige them: trading blows with a foe who has nothing left to lose is the meanest tactic in the canon.

sentences.zh: 吾將以計取之。

translations.literal: I will by stratagem take him.
translations.idiomatic: He would take Fu Deng by stratagem instead.

sentences.zh: 」於是留其尚書令姚旻守安定，夜襲登輜重於大界，克之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left his Grand Secretary Yao Min to guard Anding and night-raided Deng's baggage train at Dajie; overcame it.
translations.idiomatic: He left Grand Secretary Yao Min to hold Anding and struck Deng's baggage park at Dajie by night, taking it whole.

sentences.zh: 諸將或欲因登駭亂擊之，萇曰：「登眾雖亂，怒氣猶盛，未可輕也。

translations.literal: Some generals wished to strike him taking advantage of Deng's panic disorder; Chang said, "Though Deng's host is disorderly, angry qi is still abundant—not can treat lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged a strike while Deng reeled. Yao Chang held them back: "His ranks may waver, but their rage still burns—do not underestimate them."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He held his hand.

sentences.zh: 萇以安定地狹，且逼苻登，使姚碩德鎮安定，徙安定千餘家安于陰密，遣弟征南靖鎮之。

translations.literal: Chang because Anding land was narrow and moreover pressed by Fu Deng, made Yao Shuode garrison Anding, relocated Anding more than a thousand households to settle at Yinmi, sent younger brother Zheng-nan Jing to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Anding was too tight against Fu Deng, so Yao Chang stationed Yao Shuode there, moved thirteen hundred families into Yinmi for safety, and sent his brother Yao Jing—the southern commander—to hold the new line.

sentences.zh: 立社稷于長安。

translations.literal: He established the altars of soil and grain at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the altars of soil and grain at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 百姓年七十有德行者，拜為中大夫，歲賜牛酒。

translations.literal: Commoners seventy years old who had virtue and conduct were appointed Palace Gentlemen; yearly oxen and wine were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners seventy years of age who were known for virtue received appointment as Palace Gentlemen, with an annual gift of ox and wine.

sentences.zh: 尹緯、姚晃謂古成詵曰：「苻登窮寇，歷年未滅，奸雄鴟峙，所在糾扇，夷夏皆貳，將若之何？

translations.literal: Yin Wei and Yao Huang spoke to Gu Cheng Shen, saying, "Fu Deng is an exhausted bandit; year after year not extinguished; villain-heroes owl-perch; everywhere gather incite; barbarian and Chinese all double—what shall be done?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei and Yao Huang asked Gu Cheng Shen: "Fu Deng still staggers on year after year; predators perch on every height; rebellion sparks wherever you look; barbarian and Han alike hedge their bets—what now?"

sentences.zh: 」詵曰：「主上權略無方，信賞必罰，賢能之士，咸懷樂推，豈慮大業不成，氐賊不滅乎！

translations.literal: Shen said, "The lord's stratagems have no bounds; trustworthy rewards certain punishments; worthy able gentlemen all harbor joyful push—why worry great enterprise not accomplished, Di bandits not destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: Shen answered: "Our lord's designs know no limit; he rewards the true word and punishes without fail; every able man gladly lifts him up—why doubt the great work will finish or the Di traitors vanish!"

sentences.zh: 」緯曰：「登窮寇未滅，奸雄所在扇合，吾等寧無懼乎？

translations.literal: Wei said, "Deng exhausted bandit not extinguished; villain-heroes everywhere fan combine—we indeed without fear?
translations.idiomatic: Wei pressed him: "Deng still lives; conspirators flock in every quarter—are we not afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」詵曰：「三秦天府之國，主上十分已有其八。

translations.literal: Shen said, "The Three Qins are a heaven-storehouse state; the lord of ten parts already has eight of them.
translations.idiomatic: Shen replied: The Three Qins are heaven's granary; our lord already holds eight shares in ten.

sentences.zh: 今所在可慮者，苻登、楊定、雷惡地耳，自餘瑣瑣，焉足論哉！

translations.literal: Now those worth worrying about are Fu Deng, Yang Ding, Lei Edui only; the remaining petty-petty—how worth discussing!
translations.idiomatic: Those worth fearing now are only Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Edui; the rest are gnats beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 然惡地地狹眾寡，不足為憂。

translations.literal: Yet Edui land narrow multitude few—not enough to be worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Edui holds narrow ground and few followers—not enough to fret over.

sentences.zh: 苻登藉烏合犬羊，偷存假息，料其智勇，非至尊之匹。

translations.literal: Fu Deng relies on a rabble of stray dogs and sheep, stealing survival breath by breath; judged by wit and courage, he is no match for the August Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng clings to a mongrel horde and buys time by theft and guile; measured against him, he cannot rival your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 霸王之起，必有驅除，然後克定大業。

translations.literal: When a hegemon-king arises, there must first be clearing away (of rivals); only then can the great enterprise be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Every founding conqueror sweeps rivals aside before the realm can be settled.

sentences.zh: 昔漢、魏之興也，皆十有餘年，乃能一同於海內，五六年間未為久也。

translations.literal: In the rise of Han and Wei, each needed more than ten years to unify the realm; five or six years is hardly long.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei each took well over a decade to knit the empire together—half a dozen years is no great span.

sentences.zh: 主上神略內明，英武外發，可謂無敵於天下耳，取登有餘力。

translations.literal: Our lord is illumined within by divine stratagem and fierce without in martial display—he may be called without peer under heaven; crushing Deng lies well within his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reads situations inwardly and strikes outwardly with unmatched force; Fu Deng is well within your grasp.

sentences.zh: 願布德行仁，招賢納士，厲兵秣馬，以候天機。

translations.literal: I pray you spread virtue and practice benevolence, summon worthies and gather scholars, sharpen arms and feed horses, and await Heaven's appointed moment.
translations.idiomatic: Spread virtue, recruit talent, drill the army and provision the horses, and watch for the turning tide.

sentences.zh: 如其鴻業不成者，詵請腰斬以謝明公。

translations.literal: If this grand enterprise then fails, I, Shen, ask to be cut at the waist to apologize before you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Should the great cause miscarry, I ask to die halved at the waist as amends to you.

sentences.zh: 」緯言之於萇，萇大悅，賜詵爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Yin Wei relayed this to Chang; Chang was greatly pleased and ennobled Shen as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Wei reported Gu Cheng Shen's words to Yao Chang, he was delighted and invested Shen as Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 雷惡地率眾降萇，拜為鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Lei E'di led his followers to surrender to Chang and was appointed General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Lei E'di brought his host over and received the title General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 魏褐飛自稱大將軍、沖天王，率氐胡數萬人攻安北姚當城於杏城，雷惡地應之，攻鎮東姚漢得于李潤。

translations.literal: Wei Hefei styled himself Grand General and Prince Who Storms Heaven; he led tens of thousands of Di and Hu to attack Defender of the North Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng; Lei E'di responded to him and assaulted General Who Guards the East Yao Hande at Li Run.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hefei proclaimed himself Grand General and Celestial Invader King, marched tens of thousands of Di and Hu against Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng while Lei E'di joined him and struck Yao Hande at Li Run.

sentences.zh: 萇議將討之，群臣咸曰：「陛下不憂六十里苻登，乃憂六百里褐飛？

translations.literal: Chang debated campaigning against them; the ministers all said: "Your Majesty does not fret over Fu Deng sixty li away, yet frets over Wei Hefei six hundred li away?
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang proposed to march, his officials cried: "Fu Deng lies sixty li off—why worry about Wei Hefei six hundred li away?"

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「登非可卒殄，吾城亦非登所能卒圖。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Deng cannot be crushed overnight, nor can my cities be seized from him overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang replied: "Fu Deng will not fall in one blow, and he cannot suddenly seize my walled towns either."

sentences.zh: 惡地多智，非常人也。

translations.literal: E'di is full of stratagem—no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Lei E'di is cunning—he is no common foe.

sentences.zh: 南引褐飛，東結董成，甘言美說以成奸謀，若得杏城、李潤，惡地據之，控制遠近，相為羽翼，長安東北非復吾有。

translations.literal: Southward he draws Hefei, eastward he binds Dong Cheng; with honeyed words he completes a treacherous plot—if he takes Xingcheng and Li Run and E'di holds them, controlling far and near and pairing wings, the northeast of Chang'an will no longer be ours.
translations.idiomatic: He pulls Wei Hefei from the south, joins Dong Cheng in the east, and flatters his way through a conspiracy—should he seize Xingcheng and Li Run and Lei E'di fortify them, swaying the countryside and backing one another, we lose everything northeast of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 」於是潛軍赴之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he marched his army thither in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped an army toward them unseen.

sentences.zh: 萇時眾不滿二千，褐飛、惡地眾至數萬，氐胡赴之者首尾不絕。

translations.literal: At that time Chang's men numbered fewer than two thousand, while Hefei's and E'di's rose to tens of thousands, and Di and Hu flocking to join them formed an unbroken train.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang had under two thousand soldiers; Wei Hefei and Lei E'di mustered tens of thousands, and bands of Di and Hu kept arriving.

sentences.zh: 萇每見一軍至，輒有喜色。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang saw another host arrive, his face lit with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Each time fresh enemy troops appeared, Yao Chang looked pleased.

sentences.zh: 群下怪而問之，萇曰：「今同惡相濟，皆來會集，吾得乘勝席捲，一舉而覆其巢穴，東北無復餘也。

translations.literal: His officers wondered and questioned him; Chang said: "Now our shared foes lend one another aid and all gather together—I may ride victory to roll them up in one sweep and overturn their nest in a single blow; nothing will remain in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: His staff asked why he smiled; he said: "They are flocking to aid one another—I can sweep them in one stroke and tear out their lair; the northeast will hold no remnant."

sentences.zh: 」褐飛等以萇兵少，盡眾來攻。

translations.literal: Hefei and the others, seeing Chang's troops were few, threw their whole force into the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking Yao Chang weak in numbers, Wei Hefei threw every man forward.

sentences.zh: 萇固壘不戰，示之以弱，潛遣子崇率騎數百，出其不意，以乘其後。

translations.literal: Chang held his ramparts and refused battle, showing weakness; secretly he sent his son Chong at the head of several hundred horsemen to strike where they did not expect, hitting them from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang stayed behind his walls to seem weak, then secretly sent Yao Chong with a few hundred riders to slash their rear by surprise.

sentences.zh: 褐飛兵擾亂，萇遣鎮遠王超、平遠譚亮率步騎擊之，褐飛眾大潰，斬褐飛及首級萬餘。

translations.literal: Hefei's troops fell into confusion; Chang dispatched Wang Chao the General Who Guards the Distance and Tan Liang the General Who Pacifies the Distance with infantry and cavalry to strike them; Hefei's host routed utterly—Hefei was beheaded along with more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hefei's ranks broke; Yao Chang sent Wang Chao and Tan Liang with horse and foot to charge—Wei Hefei fell and over ten thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 惡地請降，萇待之如初。

translations.literal: E'di asked to surrender; Chang treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Lei E'di sued for peace and Yao Chang received him as he had earlier.

sentences.zh: 惡地每謂人曰：「吾自言智勇所施，足為一時之傑。

translations.literal: E'di often told people: "In what wit and daring I deploy, I am enough to stand as a champion of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lei E'di used to say: "My wit and nerve fit me to tower above my generation."

sentences.zh: 校數諸雄，如吾之徒，皆應跨據一方，獸嘯千里。

translations.literal: Measured against the heroes of the day, men like me ought to stride across a territory and roar like beasts for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Stack me against the warlords and I should rule a quarter of the realm and thunder across a thousand miles.

sentences.zh: 遇姚公智力摧屈，是吾分也。

translations.literal: Meeting Lord Yao, wit and strength were bent aside—that was my allotted portion.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yao broke my schemes—that was simply my fate.

sentences.zh: 」惡地猛毅清肅，不可幹以非義，嶺北諸豪皆敬憚之。

translations.literal: E'di was fierce, resolute, austere, and upright—no wrongful plea could sway him; all the magnates north of the ridges both revered and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Lei E'di was grim, upright, and incorruptible—nothing unjust could move him; every strongman beyond the ranges feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功。

translations.literal: Chang ordered his general Dangcheng to plant one tree in a single lattice hole at the camp site, to mark the battle honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang told General Yao Dangcheng to set one sapling in a picket hole at the battlefield camp as a trophy.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，問之，城曰：「營所至小，已廣之矣。

translations.literal: More than a year later he asked him; Dangcheng said: "The camp ground was small—I have already enlarged it.
translations.idiomatic: When asked a year later, Dangcheng said: "The plot was cramped—I have widened it."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「少來鬥戰無如此快，以千六百人破三萬眾，國之事業，由此克舉。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Never in skirmishing have I felt such ease—sixteen hundred men broke thirty thousand; the state's enterprise hangs on victories like this.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang answered: "No fight ever pleased me more—sixteen hundred broke thirty thousand; our dynasty turns on blows like that."

sentences.zh: 小乃為奇，大何足貴！」

translations.literal: Small becomes marvelous—what good is mere size!"
translations.idiomatic: Small numbers becoming supreme—that is the marvel; sheer bulk counts for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 貳城胡曹寅、王達獻馬三千匹。

translations.literal: The Hu of Ercheng, Cao Yin and Wang Da, presented three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yin and Wang Da of the Hu in Ercheng offered three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 以寅為鎮北將軍、并州刺史，達鎮遠將軍、金城太守。

translations.literal: Yin was made General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Bing Province; Da became General Who Guards the Distance and prefect of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yin took office as General Who Guards the North and inspector of Bing; Wang Da as General Who Guards the Distance and prefect of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 萇性簡率，群下有過，或面加罵辱。

translations.literal: Chang's nature was blunt and forthright; when subordinates erred, he would sometimes berate them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang was plainspoken—when followers slipped, he often cursed them publicly.

sentences.zh: 太常權翼言於萇曰：「陛下弘達自任，不修小節，駕馭群雄，苞羅俊異，棄嫌錄善，有高祖之量。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Quan Yi said to Chang: "Your Majesty is magnanimous and self-trusting, heedless of petty niceties; you rein in the heroes, embrace the talented and strange, set aside grudges and record virtue—you have the capacity of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi told him: "You trust yourself broadly and scorn small etiquette; you harness champions and gather odd talents, forgiving old slights—that is Gaozu's breadth."

sentences.zh: 然輕慢之風，所宜除也。

translations.literal: Yet the manner of careless contempt ought to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: But the habit of casual contempt must go.

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「吾之性也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "That is my nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang said: "That is simply how I am."

sentences.zh: 吾於舜之美，未有片焉；

translations.literal: As for Shun's excellences, I possess not a shard;
translations.idiomatic: I own no shred of Shun's virtues;

sentences.zh: 漢祖之短，已收其一。

translations.literal: of Han Gaozu's shortcomings, I have already collected one.
translations.idiomatic: of Han Gaozu's faults I have already taken one.

sentences.zh: 若不聞讜言，安知過也！」

translations.literal: If I did not hear blunt counsel, how would I know my faults!"
translations.idiomatic: Had I no frank words, how would I see my errors?"

sentences.zh: 南羌竇鴦率戶五千來降，拜安西將軍。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan of the southern Qiang led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan of the southern Qiang brought five thousand households over and became General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 萇下書，有復私仇者，皆誅之。

translations.literal: Chang issued an edict: whoever avenged private wrongs would all be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang decreed death for anyone settling private blood-feuds.

sentences.zh: 將吏亡滅者，各隨所親以立後，振給長育之。

translations.literal: For commanders and clerks who had died, each household was to establish an heir according to kinship and receive relief to raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Where officers or clerks had perished, heirs were named by nearest kin and supported to maturity.

sentences.zh: 鎮東苟曜據逆萬堡，密引苻登。

translations.literal: Gou Yao the General Who Guards the East held Niwan Fort and secretly drew in Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao, General Who Guards the East, occupied Niwan Fort and secretly welcomed Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 萇與登戰，敗于馬頭原，收眾復戰。

translations.literal: Chang fought Deng and was defeated at Matou Plain; he gathered his troops and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang clashed with Fu Deng, lost at Matou Plain, regrouped, and renewed the battle.

sentences.zh: 姚碩德謂諸將曰：「上慎于輕戰，每欲以計取之。

translations.literal: Yao Shuode said to the generals: "The sovereign is cautious about rash battle—he always wishes to take the foe by stratagem.
