translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode told the commanders: "Our lord hates reckless fights and prefers to win by craft."

sentences.zh: 今戰既失利，而更逼賊者，必有由也。

translations.literal: Now that battle has already miscarried yet he presses the enemy harder, there must be a reason.
translations.idiomatic: Now he charges again after a setback—there has to be a motive.

sentences.zh: 」萇聞而謂碩德曰：「登用兵遲緩，不識虛實，今輕兵直進，逕據吾東，必苟曜豎子與之連結也。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Chang said to Shuode: "Fu Deng's deployments are sluggish—he does not grasp void and substance; now light troops push straight forward and seize our eastern flank outright—it must be that stripling Gou Yao has linked with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang heard and explained to Shuode: "Fu Deng moves slowly and misreads the field; light forces racing east mean that pup Gou Yao has joined him."

sentences.zh: 事久變成，其禍難測。

translations.literal: If matters drag on and shift, the harm cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Delay turns peril unknowable.

sentences.zh: 所以速戰者，欲使豎子謀之未就，好之未深，散敗其事耳。

translations.literal: The reason I strike quickly is to catch the stripling before his plot ripens and his favors deepen—to scatter and wreck his enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I strike fast so the wretch's scheme barely forms and his ties stay shallow—I mean to break his plan outright.

sentences.zh: 」進戰，大敗之，登退屯於郿。

translations.literal: He advanced to battle and routed Deng utterly; Deng withdrew and encamped at Mei.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack, shattered Fu Deng, and Deng fell back to Mei.

sentences.zh: 登將金槌以新平降萇，萇輕將數百騎入槌營。

translations.literal: Deng's officer Jin Chui surrendered Xiping to Chang; Chang rode several hundred horsemen lightly into Chui's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's general Jin Chui yielded Xiping; Yao Chang entered Chui's camp with only a few hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 群下諫之，萇曰：「槌既去苻登，復欲圖我，將安所歸！

translations.literal: His ministers remonstrated; Chang said: "If Chui has left Fu Deng and again plots against me, where else can he turn!
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers protested; Yao Chang said: "If Jin Chui has quit Fu Deng yet schemes against me, where can he run?"

sentences.zh: 且懷德初附，推款委質，吾復以不信待之，何以禦物乎！

translations.literal: Moreover at first attachment one lays open good faith and pledges allegiance—if I greet that with distrust, how shall I command the world!
translations.idiomatic: Men first joining lay down good faith—if I meet them with suspicion, how do I lead anyone?"

sentences.zh: 」群氐果有異謀，槌不從而止。

translations.literal: The mass of Di indeed harbored a plot, but Chui would not follow and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Di did plot treason, yet Jin Chui refused and the plot died.

sentences.zh: 萇如陰密攻登，敕其太子興曰：「苟曜好奸變，將為國害，聞吾還北，必來見汝，汝便執之。

translations.literal: Chang went to Yinmi to attack Deng and instructed Crown Prince Xing: "Gou Yao delights in treacherous shifts—he will harm the state; when he hears I have turned north he is sure to visit you—then seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang marched on Yinmi against Fu Deng and warned Crown Prince Yao Xing: "Gou Yao is a shifty traitor—when he hears I am riding north he will call on you; arrest him."

sentences.zh: 」苟曜果見興于長安，興遣尹緯讓而誅之。

translations.literal: Gou Yao indeed appeared before Xing in Chang'an; Xing sent Yin Wei to rebuke him and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao came to Yao Xing at Chang'an; Xing had Yin Wei denounce him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 萇大敗登于安定東，置酒高會，諸將咸曰：「若值魏武王，不令此賊至今，陛下將牢太過耳。

translations.literal: Chang utterly defeated Deng east of Anding and held a lofty banquet; the generals all said: "Had we met Emperor Wu of Wei, we would not have let this bandit survive to today—Your Majesty has simply been too cautious.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing Fu Deng east of Anding, Yao Chang feasted his officers; they said: "Had Wei Wu lived this rebel would not endure—you have hedged too much."

sentences.zh: 」萇笑曰：「吾不如亡兄有四：身長八尺五寸，臂垂過膝，人望而畏之，一也；

translations.literal: Chang laughed and said: "I fall short of my late brother in four things: eight chi five cun in height, arms hanging past the knees—men shrink at the sight—first;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang laughed: "I trail my dead brother in four ways: eight feet five inches tall, arms past the knees—men quail—that is one;

sentences.zh: 當十萬之眾，與天下爭衡，望麾而進，前無橫陣，二也；

translations.literal: facing a hundred thousand massed he strove with the realm for mastery—his banner advanced and no ranked line blocked him—second;
translations.idiomatic: with a hundred thousand under him he wrestled the empire—his standard moved and no formation barred him—two;

sentences.zh: 溫古知今，講論道藝，駕馭英雄，收羅雋異，三也；

translations.literal: warming to antiquity and knowing the present, discoursing on the Way and arts, harnessing heroes and gathering the extraordinary—third;
translations.idiomatic: mastering past and present, discussing doctrine and craft, yoking heroes and rare talents—three;

sentences.zh: 董率大眾，履險若夷，上下咸允，人盡死力，四也。

translations.literal: marshaling great hosts, treading peril as if flat—high and low alike approved and every man gave his life—four.
translations.idiomatic: leading vast armies through danger as on level ground—every rank trusted him and men died willingly—four.

sentences.zh: 所以得建立功業，策任群賢者，正望算略中一片耳。

translations.literal: That I could establish achievements and assign worthies rests solely on a fragment of calculation among them.
translations.idiomatic: What lets me build merit and seat wise men is only a sliver of their planning.

sentences.zh: 」群臣咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers all shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The court cried "Long live your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 萇下書令留台諸鎮各置學官，勿有所廢，考試優劣，隨才擢敘。

translations.literal: Chang issued an edict ordering every garrison of the rear headquarters to install school officers without abolishing any, examine merit and fault, and promote according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered each rear-base command to keep schools staffed, test pupils, and promote by ability.

sentences.zh: 苻登驃騎將軍沒奕于率戶六千降，拜使持節、車騎將軍、高平公。

translations.literal: Fu Deng's Grand Marshal Moyijian led six thousand households to surrender and was appointed credential-bearing General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Moyijian, Fu Deng's Grand Marshal of Agile Cavalry, brought six thousand households over and received credentials as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 萇寢疾，遣姚碩德鎮李潤，尹緯守長安，召其太子興詣行營。

translations.literal: When Chang lay gravely ill he sent Yao Shuode to hold Li Run, Yin Wei to guard Chang'an, and summoned Crown Prince Xing to the field camp.
translations.idiomatic: Gravely ill, Yao Chang stationed Yao Shuode at Li Run, Yin Wei at Chang'an, and called Crown Prince Yao Xing to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 征南姚方成言於興曰：「今寇賊未滅，上復寢疾，王統、苻胤等皆有部曲，終為人害，宜盡除之。

translations.literal: Yao Fangcheng the General Who Conquers the South said to Xing: "Bandits are not yet destroyed and the sovereign again lies ill; Wang Tong, Fu Yin, and the rest all retain private troops—they will end as a threat and ought all to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Fangcheng warned Yao Xing: "Enemies remain and the emperor sickens—Wang Tong and Fu Yin still command retinues and will become dangers; purge them."

sentences.zh: 」興於是誅苻胤、王統、王廣、徐成、毛盛，乃赴召。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon executed Fu Yin, Wang Tong, Wang Guang, Xu Cheng, and Mao Sheng, then answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing slew Fu Yin, Wang Tong, Wang Guang, Xu Cheng, and Mao Sheng, then rode to camp.

sentences.zh: 興至，萇怒曰：「王統兄弟是吾州裏，無他遠志，徐成等昔在秦朝，並為名將。

translations.literal: When Xing arrived, Chang angrily said: "The Wang brothers are men of my province without distant ambition; Xu Cheng and the others were famed generals under Former Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing came, Yao Chang thundered: "The Wang brothers are fellow townsmen without wider aims; Xu Cheng and company were Former Qin's renowned captains.

sentences.zh: 天下小定，吾方任之，奈何輒便誅害，令人喪氣！」

translations.literal: With the realm nearly settled I was about to employ them—how could you slaughter them outright and break men's spirits!"
translations.idiomatic: Peace was almost within reach—I meant to use them—why kill them and chill every heart?"

sentences.zh: 萇下書，兵吏從征伐，戶在大營者，世世復其家，無所豫。

translations.literal: Chang issued an edict: soldiers and clerks who followed campaigns—households enrolled in the great camp—were exempted forever from levy, without exception.
translations.idiomatic: His edict exempted forever every soldier's household registered in the main camp from service.

sentences.zh: 苻登與竇沖相持，萇議擊之，尹緯言於萇曰：「太子純厚之稱，著于遐邇，將領英略，未為遠近所知。

translations.literal: Fu Deng locked horns with Dou Chong; Chang debated striking him. Yin Wei said to Chang: "The Crown Prince bears a reputation for pure sincerity renowned afar; his martial talent is not yet known near and far.
translations.idiomatic: While Fu Deng faced Dou Chong, Yao Chang weighed an attack. Yin Wei said: "The heir is famed for kindness far and wide but his generalship is still unknown."

sentences.zh: 宜遣太子親行，可以漸廣威武，防窺窬之原。

translations.literal: You ought to send the Crown Prince in person—it can gradually broadcast martial prestige and shut the door to intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch the heir himself—that spreads martial awe and blocks plots early.

sentences.zh: 」萇從之，戎興曰：「賊徒知汝轉近，必相驅入堡，聚而掩之，無不克矣。

translations.literal: Chang agreed and instructed Xing: "When the brigands know you draw near they will surely herd into forts—gather and envelop them—none will escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang agreed and told Yao Xing: "When bandits sense you closing they will cram into stockades—surround and swallow them—none survive.

sentences.zh: 」比至胡空堡，沖圍自解。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Konghu Fort, Chong's siege lifted of itself.
translations.idiomatic: When he neared Konghu Fort, Dou Chong's siege collapsed on its own.

sentences.zh: 登聞興向胡空堡，引還，興因襲平涼，大獲而歸，咸如萇策。

translations.literal: Deng heard Xing was heading for Konghu Fort and withdrew; Xing then raided Pingliang and returned laden with spoils—everything matched Chang's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng pulled back on news of Yao Xing; Yao Xing struck Pingliang and returned heavy with booty—just as Yao Chang predicted.

sentences.zh: 使興還鎮長安。

translations.literal: He had Xing return to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Xing back to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 萇下書除妖謗之言及赦前奸穢，有相劾舉者，皆以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: Chang issued an edict: rumors of sorcery and slander and prior unpardoned villainies—whoever impeaches another on such grounds suffers the same crime.
translations.idiomatic: He banned accusations founded on tales of witchcraft or old unpardoned crimes—the accuser suffers the accused's penalty.

sentences.zh: 晉平遠將軍、護氐校尉楊佛嵩率胡蜀三千餘戶降于萇，晉將楊佺期、趙睦追之。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Pacifies the Distance and Colonel Protecting the Di, Yang Fosong, led more than three thousand Hu and Shu households to surrender to Chang; Jin generals Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fosong, Jin's distant-pacifying general and Di colonel, brought three thousand Shu and Hu households to Yao Chang; Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu gave chase.

sentences.zh: 遣姚崇赴救，大敗晉師，斬趙睦。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Chong to rescue; he routed the Jin army utterly and beheaded Zhao Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Yao Chong, shattered the Jin force, and killed Zhao Mu.

sentences.zh: 以佛嵩為鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Fosong General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fosong became General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 萇如長安，至於新支堡，疾篤，輿疾而進。

translations.literal: Chang went to Chang'an; when he reached Xinchi Fort he grew desperately ill and had himself carried forward in the litter.
translations.idiomatic: Bound for Chang'an, he fell desperately ill at Xinchi Fort and was borne onward in his carriage.

sentences.zh: 夢苻堅將天官使者、鬼兵數百突入營中，萇懼，走入宮，宮人迎萇刺鬼，誤中萇陰，鬼相謂曰：「正中死處。

translations.literal: He dreamed Fu Jian dispatched celestial officers and hundreds of ghost soldiers bursting into the camp; Chang fled in terror into the palace; palace women welcomed Chang and stabbed the ghosts but mistakenly struck Chang's groin; the ghosts said to one another: "Right in the fatal spot.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed Fu Jian sent celestial envoys and hundreds of ghost warriors storming his camp; fleeing into the harem, women stabbed at ghosts but pierced his groin; the spirits murmured: "Dead center.

sentences.zh: 」拔矛，出血石餘。

translations.literal: They drew the lance—blood flowed more than a stone's measure.
translations.idiomatic: They pulled the spear free and blood gushed over a peck.

sentences.zh: 寤而驚悸，遂患陰腫，醫刺之，出血如夢。

translations.literal: Awakening with a start, he grew swollen in the groin; physicians lanced it and blood flowed as in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: He woke in panic; his groin swelled; doctors lanced it and blood flowed as in the nightmare.

sentences.zh: 萇遂狂言，或稱「臣萇，殺陛下者兄襄，非臣之罪，願不枉臣。

translations.literal: Chang then raved, sometimes declaring "Your subject Chang—your Majesty's killer was elder brother Xiang, not your subject; I beg you not to wrong your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yao Chang raved, crying that brother Yao Xiang had slain Fu Jian, not he—begging the throne not to blame him.

sentences.zh: 」至長安，召太尉姚旻、尚書左僕射尹緯、右僕射姚晃、尚書狄伯支等入，受遺輔政。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an he summoned Grand Commandant Yao Min, Left Secretary Director Yin Wei, Right Secretary Director Yao Huang, Secretary Di Bozhi, and others, and received their testamentary duty to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an he called in Yao Min, Yin Wei, Yao Huang, Di Bozhi, and others to accept charge as regents.

sentences.zh: 萇謂興曰：「有毀此諸人者，慎勿受之。

translations.literal: Chang said to Xing: "If anyone slanders these men, take care not to heed it.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yao Xing: "If anyone defames these ministers, do not listen.

sentences.zh: 汝撫骨肉以仁，接大臣以禮，待物以信，遇黔首以恩，四者既備，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: Treat flesh-and-blood kin with benevolence, great ministers with ritual propriety, affairs with good faith, and the black-haired people with kindness—when these four are ready, I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: Cherish kin with kindness, greet ministers with courtesy, handle affairs with trust, and rule commoners with grace—once those four stand firm I need fear nothing.

sentences.zh: 」乙太元十八年死，時年六十四，在位八年。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of the Taiyuan era he died, aged sixty-four, having reigned eight years.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era at the age of sixty-four after eight years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 偽諡武昭皇帝，廟號太祖，墓稱原陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled falsely Emperor Wu Zhao; his temple name was Taizu; his tomb was called Yuanling.
translations.idiomatic: They gave him the Later Qin posthumous title Emperor Wuzhao, temple name Taizu, tomb name Yuanling.
